payload: A strengthening 'super' El Nino (record-warming Pacific waters, comparable to 2015) is suppressing the Atlantic hurricane season with wind shear and dry air -- only 3 named storms so far, with maybe 5-6 more expected -- while firing up an extremely active Pacific with ~7 tropical systems (including a Fujiwhara-effect pair) and one Atlantic area, likely soon-to-be Tropical Storm Dolly near the Lesser Antilles. Domestically it has locked a heat dome over the Southern Plains/Desert Southwest (100s in Dallas, record heat in Arizona/SoCal) while northwesterly flow keeps the Midwest/Northeast below average; late August brings 25-35 degrees above average to the Great Plains, then a Tuesday/Wednesday cold front and rising uncertainty in the second week of September. Looking ahead, the winter storm track is expected to shift south, making for an active winter across Dixie Alley, the Southern Plains, and the East Coast.
notes: Atlantic: currently ~1 area of development, likely to become Tropical Storm Dolly within 24h near/east of the Lesser Antilles; if any Atlantic system does organize it could rapidly intensify to a major hurricane given very warm, untouched waters.
Pacific: 4 active areas, 1 tropical storm + 3 depressions plus a possible typhoon near China; a Fujiwhara effect (two lows orbiting/merging) will occur in the western Pacific but not hit land.

Early September: heat dome shifts to the Central Plains/Midwest/Tennessee Valley, jet stream lifts, severe weather returns to the Northern Plains (some into Midwest/Great Lakes); possible first Rockies snow; a big pattern-breaking storm system likely within 1-2 weeks.

Temperature outlook: 25-30 above average building late August, 30-35 above average Oklahoma City to Minneapolis/Wisconsin by early next week; GFS keeps heat until ~mid-September then hints at a large cold shot, but model runs are highly variable.
A separate 'first winter forecast' video is teased for ~first week of September.
